title: Paddy Nitrogen and Zinc Deficiency Management
content: Yellowing of older lower leaves in paddy typically indicates nitrogen deficiency, whereas rusty brown spots or chlorosis on younger leaves indicates zinc deficiency (Khaira disease). Farmers should verify water levels, inspect root health for sulphide toxicity or root rot, and apply recommended top-dressing of urea in split doses or zinc sulphate (0.5% foliar spray with lime) if zinc deficiency is diagnosed.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad & UAS Bangalore Package of Practices

title: Paddy Yellow Stem Borer Management
content: Yellow Stem Borer larvae bore into the central tiller causing dead hearts during vegetative stage and white ears (white heads) at heading stage. Management includes clipping seedling leaf tips before transplanting, setting up pheromone traps @ 5/acre, conserving natural parasitoids like Trichogramma, and applying recommended threshold-based chemical granules like Cartap hydrochloride 4G or Chlorantraniliprole when pest pressure exceeds economic threshold.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR) - Integrated Pest Management Guidelines

title: Ragi Moisture Stress and Drought Management
content: During prolonged dry spells or delayed rainfall, ragi (finger millet) crops exhibit leaf curling, premature drying, and wilting. Protective measures include providing protective life-saving irrigation at tillering or flowering stages if water is available, spraying 1% potassium chloride (KCl) or 2% urea to reduce transpiration shock, maintaining inter-cultivation soil mulching to conserve root zone moisture, and practicing clean weeding to eliminate moisture competition.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Bangalore - Dryland Agriculture Technical Bulletin

title: Ragi Blast Disease (Pyricularia grisea) Management
content: Ragi blast affects leaves (spindle-shaped lesions with grey centers), nodes (blackened rotting), and neck/fingers (grain sterility). Management involves using resistant cultivars (like GPU-28, ML-365), treating seeds with Carbendazim (2g/kg seed), avoiding excess nitrogen fertilization, and applying preventive sprays of Tricyclazole 75 WP (0.6g/L) or Mancozeb if weather is overcast with high humidity.
source: All India Coordinated Research Project on Small Millets (AICRP-ICAR), Bengaluru

title: Maize Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) Management
content: Fall Armyworm causes characteristic ragged pinholes, windowing on leaves, and heavy fecal frass inside the central whorl. Management includes deep summer ploughing, installing pheromone traps @ 4/acre for monitoring, handpicking egg masses, applying Neem oil (Azadirachtin 1500 ppm @ 5ml/L) or Metarhizium anisopliae early, and whorl application of Emamectin benzoate 5% SG (0.4g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC (0.4ml/L) during severe early-to-mid whorl stages.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana & ICAR-NBAIR Bengaluru

title: Maize Waterlogging and Excess Rainfall Management
content: Maize is highly sensitive to waterlogging, especially in seedling and knee-high stages. Prolonged standing water causes root asphyxiation, nutrient leaching, and stunting. Farmers must dig drainage furrows immediately to remove stagnant water, apply a foliar spray of 1-2% urea or DAP once field drains to stimulate root recovery, and inspect for secondary bacterial stalk rot infections.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR) - Agronomy Advisory

title: Groundnut Tikka Leaf Spot Management
content: Tikka leaf spot (Cercospora arachidicola / Cercosporidium personatum) produces dark brown-to-black circular spots with yellow halos on older leaves, leading to severe defoliation. Recommended practices include crop rotation, seed treatment with Trichoderma viride or Thiram (3g/kg), and foliar application of Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Carbendazim (1g/L) or Hexaconazole (1ml/L) at the onset of spot appearance.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Groundnut Research (DGR), Junagadh

title: Groundnut White Grub Management
content: White grub (Holotrichia consanguinea) larvae feed on rootlets and pod pegs, causing patchy wilting and sudden drying of standing groundnut plants. Management involves light trap catches of adult beetles after monsoon showers, seed treatment with Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (2ml/kg), application of well-decomposed FYM (avoiding raw manure), and soil drenching with Chlorpyrifos 20 EC if grub attack is identified in active patches.
source: University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad - Oilseeds Advisory

title: Sugarcane Early Shoot Borer Management
content: Early Shoot Borer (Chilo infuscatellus) attacks 1-3 month old cane shoots producing central dead hearts that pull out easily with an unpleasant odour. Management involves trash mulching @ 3 tonnes/acre in cane rows, earthing-up operations at 45 days, releasing Trichogramma chilonis egg parasitoids, and soil application of Cartap hydrochloride 4G or Chlorantraniliprole 0.4% GR along the rows before irrigation.
source: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore

title: Sugarcane Red Rot Disease Prevention
content: Red rot (Colletotrichum falcatum) causes yellowing and drying of the third or fourth leaf from crown, longitudinal reddening of internal stalk tissues with crosswise white patches, and sour alcoholic smell. Control relies strictly on planting certified disease-free sets, practicing set treatment with Carbendazim (0.1%) hot water treatment, burning infected stubbles, maintaining crop rotation with rice, and avoiding flood irrigation from infected plots.
source: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore

title: Cotton Pink Bollworm and Sucking Pest Management
content: Pink bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) damages squares and bolls, leading to rosetted flowers and stained lint. Sucking pests (thrips, aphids, jassids) cause leaf crinkling and curling. Integrated control includes pheromone trapping @ 8-10/acre, destruction of rosette flowers, conserving predatory ladybird beetles, installing yellow/blue sticky traps, and rotating insecticides (Neem formulations, Flonicamid 50 WG, or Spinetoram 11.7 SC) when thresholds are crossed.
source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur

title: Cotton Waterlogging Reddening and Foliar Nutrition
content: Excess rainfall and prolonged soil saturation cause cotton leaf yellowing, bronzing/reddening, and square shedding due to poor nitrogen and magnesium uptake. Immediate field drainage is necessary. After water recedes, spray 1% Magnesium Sulphate (MgSO4) + 1% Urea or 19:19:19 balanced fertilizer at 10-day intervals to restore chlorophyll synthesis and retain fruiting branches.
source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur - Crop Advisory

title: Chilli Leaf Curl and Thrips/Mites Management
content: Chilli leaf curling is predominantly caused by Thrips (leaves curl upwards with boat-shaped appearance) or Mites (leaves curl downwards with elongation). Control includes erecting blue sticky traps for thrips and yellow sticky traps for whiteflies @ 15/acre, spraying neem cake extract or Pongamia oil, and applying targeted acaricides/insecticides like Diafenthiuron 50 WP (1g/L), Spiromesifen 22.9 SC (1ml/L), or Fipronil 5 SC (1.5ml/L).
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: Chilli Anthracnose and Die-Back Disease Management
content: Anthracnose (Colletotrichum capsici) causes tip die-back on twigs and circular sunken necrotic lesions on ripening fruits. Recommended management includes using disease-free treated seed, avoiding overhead sprinkler irrigation, prompt removal of infected fruit, and foliar spraying of Azoxystrobin 23 SC (1ml/L) or Copper oxychloride (2.5g/L) + Streptocycline during humid conditions.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: Onion Excess Rain Drainage and Purple Blotch Control
content: Excessive rainfall in onion fields leads to root suffocation, bulb rotting, and outbreaks of Purple Blotch (Alternaria porri - water-soaked lesions that turn purplish-brown). Action steps: create immediate shallow exit drains to remove standing water, avoid applying additional nitrogen until soils dry, and spray Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5g/L) or Propiconazole 25 EC (1ml/L) combined with an agricultural sticker/spreader.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR), Pune

title: Onion Thrips (Thrips tabaci) Management
content: Onion thrips lacerate leaf tissues causing silvery white blotches and distorted curly leaf tips. Severe infestation leads to leaf drying and undersized bulb development. Management includes installing blue sticky traps @ 20/acre, sprinkler irrigation to dislodge nymphs, and spraying Profenofos 50 EC (1ml/L) or Spinosad 45 SC (0.3ml/L) directed into the leaf sheaths.
source: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR), Pune

title: Potato Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) Management
content: Late blight appears as water-soaked irregular dark brown lesions on leaf margins with white fuzzy fungal growth on leaf undersides in cold, humid weather. Rapid destruction of foliage can occur. Management requires using certified disease-free seed tubers, earthing-up to prevent tuber infection, and spraying preventive Mancozeb 75 WP (2.5g/L) followed by systemic Cymoxanil + Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Dimethomorph (1g/L) if active lesions appear.
source: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI), Shimla

title: Potato Tuber Bulking and Balanced Nutrition
content: Potato requires balanced nitrogen, phosphorus, and high potassium during the tuber bulking stage (45-70 days after planting). Excessive late nitrogen causes foliage overgrown at the expense of tuber formation. Adequate potassium (SOP/MOP) improves tuber size, starch content, and drought resistance. Ensure uniform light irrigations and avoid alternate wetting and severe drying cycles.
source: ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI), Shimla

title: Banana Potassium Deficiency and Leaf Yellowing
content: Potassium deficiency in banana is characterized by rapid yellowing of older leaf tips and margins (orange-yellow chlorosis) that curls backward and rapidly dries, while the midrib stays green. Ensure application of recommended Muriate of Potash (MOP) in 3-4 split doses during vegetative and bunch development stages, and apply organic compost to enhance potassium uptake.
source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB), Tiruchirappalli

title: Banana Panama Wilt and Sigatoka Leaf Spot
content: Panama disease (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense) causes yellowing of lower leaves along margins, petiole buckling, and longitudinal splitting of the pseudostem base. Sigatoka leaf spot causes oval spindle-shaped dark brown spots with grey centers. Management includes using tissue-cultured suckers, soil application of Trichoderma viride with neem cake, eliminating infected plants, and foliar spray of Propiconazole (1ml/L) with sticker for Sigatoka control.
source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB), Tiruchirappalli

title: Tomato Early Blight and Yellow Leaf Management
content: Yellowing of lower leaves in tomato with concentric target-board dark rings indicates Early Blight (Alternaria solani). General chlorosis without spots may indicate nitrogen shortage or root-knot nematode damage. Farmers should stake plants, practice bottom-leaf pruning to improve air circulation, avoid splash watering, and apply copper oxychloride (2.5g/L) or Mancozeb (2g/L) as protective spray.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

title: General Field Drainage and Post-Flood Crop Care
content: Excess rainfall and prolonged standing water deplete soil oxygen, weaken root hairs, and promote root-rotting fungi (Pythium, Phytophthora). Essential remedial steps: 1) Open main and lateral drainage trenches immediately. 2) Avoid heavy machine entry on wet soil to prevent compaction. 3) Once soil reaches working moisture, aerate the surface by light hoeing. 4) Apply light foliar micronutrients and avoid heavy basal fertilizer until fresh roots emerge.
source: Karnataka State Department of Agriculture (KSDA) & ICAR Advisory
